issues.display_title: Issue #87: feat(auth/me): expose has_password field to support change-password UX
issues.main_description_html:
RESULT 17/07/26

✅ Implementation: Auth Me Has Password Implementation

Scope

Adds a has_password boolean to GET /v1/auth/me so the frontend can choose the correct change-password UX.

Controller Response

File: src/controllers/v1/auth/me.go

  • Added has_password to the returned user profile.
  • Value is computed from whether the stored password hash is present:
"has_password": user.Password != "",
  • Email-registered accounts return true.
  • Google OAuth accounts without an email password return false.
  • Password hash remains excluded from the response.

Tests

File: src/controllers/v1/auth/me_test.go

  • Covers password account returning has_password: true.
  • Covers Google-style account with empty password returning has_password: false.
  • Asserts the response does not expose a password field.
  • Covers unauthorized response when no authenticated user is present.

Verification

Passed:

go test ./src/controllers/v1/auth -count=1

Full suite note:

go test ./... -count=1

Context

Frontend needs to detect whether a logged-in user has a password set (i.e. was registered via email) or not (Google OAuth account with no password hash).

This is required for the change-password flow on the profile page (see gothru-3d-floormap#256):

  • Email account → show "Old password" field
  • Google account → hide "Old password" field, show note: "Your account uses Google sign-in. Enter a new password to add email login."

Currently GET /v1/auth/me does not expose whether the user has a password. The password field is (correctly) never returned, so the frontend has no signal.

Change Required

In src/controllers/v1/auth/me.go, add has_password to the response:

"has_password": user.Password != "",

Full updated response block:

return helpers.FormatResponse(c, 200, fiber.Map{
    "message": "user profile retrieved",
    "user": fiber.Map{
        "created_at":     user.CreatedAt,
        "updated_at":     user.UpdatedAt,
        "name":           user.Name,
        "email":          user.Email,
        "avatar":         user.Avatar,
        "email_verified": user.EmailVerified,
        "has_password":   user.Password != "",
    },
}, startTime)

Acceptance Criteria

  • GET /v1/auth/me returns has_password: true for email-registered accounts
  • GET /v1/auth/me returns has_password: false for Google OAuth accounts
  • No password hash or any password data is ever exposed in the response

issues.display_title: Issue #89: feat(projects): add is_owner field to GET /v1/projects response
issues.main_description_html:
Problem

GET /v1/projects returns both owned and shared projects (via project_members), but response does not indicate which is which. Frontend cannot distinguish owner vs collaborator without extra API call.

Solution

Add is_owner bool to projectResponse, computed from project.UserID == currentUserID. No additional DB query — UserID already loaded from Find call.

Changes

  • src/action/v1/project/shared.go — add IsOwner bool to projectResponse
  • src/action/v1/project/list.go — set IsOwner = project.UserID == user.UniqueID in response loop

Acceptance Criteria

  • GET /v1/projects response includes is_owner: true/false per project
  • No extra DB queries added
  • Owned projects return is_owner: true, shared projects return is_owner: false

RESULT

Added is_owner bool to projectResponse, computed as project.UserID == currentUserID — no extra DB query, UserID already loaded from the existing Find/First call.

Files changed:

  • src/action/v1/project/shared.go — added IsOwner field + param to newProjectResponse
  • src/action/v1/project/list.go, recent.go, create.go, get.go, update.go — pass user.UniqueID at each call site

go build ./... and go vet ./... pass.

issues.display_title: Issue #90: feat(projects): add is_complete column to projects table
issues.main_description_html:
Overview

Add a new boolean column is_complete to the projects table. All existing rows must be backfilled to true.

Changes Required

1. Model (src/models/models.go)

Add field to Project struct:

IsComplete bool `gorm:"default:false" json:"is_complete"`

2. SQL Migration (migrations/)

Create file 202507XXXXXX_projects_is_complete.sql:

-- +migrate Up
ALTER TABLE public.projects ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS is_complete BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT false;

-- Backfill: all existing projects are considered complete
UPDATE public.projects SET is_complete = true;

-- +migrate Down
ALTER TABLE public.projects DROP COLUMN IF EXISTS is_complete;

ADD COLUMN … DEFAULT false sets the default for new rows. The explicit UPDATE backfills all existing rows to true. AutoMigrate handles the struct change but does NOT run the backfill — the cmd/migrate runner must be used for that.

Acceptance Criteria

  • is_complete column exists in projects table with DEFAULT false
  • Project struct includes IsComplete bool with correct GORM and JSON tags
  • SQL migration runs cleanly via go run ./cmd/migrate -- up
  • All pre-existing rows have is_complete = true after migration
  • New projects default to is_complete = false

API changes are out of scope for this issue.

RESULT

Added is_complete column to projects table.

Files changed:

  • src/models/models.go — added IsComplete bool with gorm:"not null;default:false" and json:"is_complete"
  • migrations/202607200001_add_is_complete_to_projects.sql — ALTER TABLE public.projects ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS is_complete BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT false + backfill UPDATE public.projects SET is_complete = true

Commits: 7fd6f4e (feat) · 2c8f297 (fix: align migration with project conventions — add -- +migrate Up directive, public. schema prefix, NOT NULL tag)

issues.display_title: Issue #91: feat(projects): allow PATCH /projects/:id to update is_complete
issues.main_description_html:
Overview

Extend the PATCH /v1/projects/:id endpoint to accept is_complete (bool) in the request body and persist it to the database.

Depends on: #90 (column must exist first).

Change Required

src/action/v1/project/update.go — add one block inside the dbUpdates mapping section, following the existing pattern:

if isComplete, ok := updates["isComplete"].(bool); ok {
    dbUpdates["is_complete"] = isComplete
}

That's the only change. Auth, permission check (role.CanWrite()), and DB write flow are already handled.

Request Example

PATCH /v1/projects/:id
{
  "isComplete": true
}

Acceptance Criteria

  • PATCH /v1/projects/:id with {"isComplete": true} sets is_complete = true in DB
  • PATCH /v1/projects/:id with {"isComplete": false} sets is_complete = false in DB
  • Omitting isComplete from body leaves existing value unchanged
  • Existing fields (name, status, etc.) unaffected
  • Requires owner or editor role (no auth changes needed — already enforced)

RESULT

Extended PATCH /v1/projects/:id to accept and persist isComplete bool.

Files changed:

  • src/action/v1/project/update.go — added isComplete key handling in dbUpdates map
  • src/action/v1/project/shared.go — exposed is_complete in project response shape
  • src/models/models.go — IsComplete field (coordinated with #90 migration fix)

Commits: 027dcbb (feat) · c18f4e8 (chore: resolve merge conflict with development — keep NOT NULL constraint)

issues.display_title: Issue #92: feat(projects): filter list to only return is_complete = true projects
issues.main_description_html:
Overview

GET /v1/projects must only return projects where is_complete = true. Projects still being set up (default false) should not appear in the list.

Depends on: #90 (column must exist), #91 (optional — for toggling).

Change Required

src/action/v1/project/list.go — add a fixed filter on line 36, right after the ownership subquery is applied:

// own + shared projects
memberProjectIDs := config.DB.Model(&models.ProjectMember{}).
    Select("project_id").
    Where("user_id = ?", user.UniqueID)
q := config.DB.Where("user_id = ? OR id IN (?)", user.UniqueID, memberProjectIDs)

// only surface completed projects
q = q.Where("is_complete = ?", true)   // ← add this line

No other changes needed.

Behaviour

is_complete Appears in list?
true ✅ yes
false (default for new projects) ❌ no

Existing filters (status, search, sort) continue to work as-is on top of this base filter.

Acceptance Criteria

  • GET /v1/projects returns only rows with is_complete = true
  • Projects with is_complete = false are invisible to the list endpoint
  • status, search, and sort query params still work correctly
  • Backfilled existing projects (is_complete = true from #90) appear normally

RESULT

Filtered GET /v1/projects to only return is_complete = true projects.

Files changed:

  • src/action/v1/project/list.go — added hardcoded q.Where("is_complete = ?", true) after ownership subquery (replaces earlier opt-in ?is_complete query param approach)

Commits: 7cecfd9 (feat: add is_complete filter) · 7fc16ad (fix: make filter hardcoded — hide incomplete projects by default)

issues.display_title: Issue #97: Recent projects: filter is_complete like the All-projects list (FE bug #333)
issues.main_description_html:
Assignee: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

Fix task for FE bug report GoThruMedia/gothru-3d-floormap#333 (deleted/abandoned project still appearing in the dashboard Recent tiles).

Root cause

GET /v1/projects (src/action/v1/project/list.go) filters is_complete = true, hiding abandoned wizard drafts from All projects. GET /v1/projects/recent (src/action/v1/project/recent.go) applies no is_complete filter, so those same drafts keep appearing as Recent tiles — the dashboard shows tiles for projects the All list says don't exist. (Soft-deleted rows are already excluded by GORM on both.)

Scope

  • Add the is_complete = true condition to the Recent query so Recent visibility matches the All-projects list.

Acceptance criteria

  • An incomplete/abandoned draft never appears in /v1/projects/recent.
  • Deleted projects remain excluded.
  • go build ./... and go vet ./... pass.

RESULT

One-line query fix in src/action/v1/project/recent.go: the Recent query now carries AND is_complete = ? (true), mirroring list.go's All-projects visibility. Soft-deleted rows were already excluded by GORM on both endpoints; the doc comment now states all three exclusions (never-opened, soft-deleted, incomplete).

Investigated and ruled out on the FE side (gothru-3d-floormap#333): the dashboard hook already optimistically removes deleted/toggled projects from its Recent state, and both server actions fetch with cache: "no-store" — the stale tiles were purely this endpoint returning incomplete drafts. FE issue gothru-3d-floormap#341 closed as misdiagnosis in favor of this fix.

Verification — go build ./... and go vet ./... clean.
